messages.content: [Inside the basketball of 'One Tree Hill' 23 years later] Actor James Lafferty (23) signals to his teammates during a basketball game hosted by Friends With Benefit commemorating the 23rd anniversary of One Tree Hill at the UNCW's Trask Coliseum on Sept. 19. Rachel Jessen for ESPN Tory Cabrera Sep 23, 2026, 08:57 AM ET Close Tory Cabrera is a writer/editor for ESPN.com who covers what' trending in the world of sports and the intersection of sports x pop culture. She hails from northern Virginia and is a graduate of UConn. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions WILMINGTON, N.C. -- "Are you here for the big game?" my new friend behind the car rental counter asked shortly after I touched down in Michael Jordan's hometown. "People are saying you need to be in line by 7 a.m. if you want a chance at a decent seat," she exclaimed before I could answer. To my surprise, my big game and her big game were one and the same: the "Hey 23" basketball game celebrating 23 years since the hit television show "One Tree Hill" first aired. Pausing to look around Wilmington International Airport, it appeared nearly everyone arriving in town had the same purpose. Couples, families and groups of friends of all ages -- all donning black, white and royal blue, and not of the Duke Blue Devils variety. I had counted at least seven combined "Scott" jerseys and two red Quentin Fields-inspired capes before a handmade "You can't kill Dan Scott" sign diverted my attention. Then the same cheerful voice snapped me back into focus. "Your car is ready. Just head to spot No. 23! See you tomorrow!" Unclear whether my rental assignment was intentional or an omen, I grabbed the keys and stepped out into the North Carolina heat. If a 23rd anniversary feels arbitrary, you're clearly not a "One Tree Hill" fan.
